title: Baron of Aberdeen: four senses of fiducia — persuasion, rest, fortitude, peace
source_text: LVIII. Sed omnium accuratissime mentem suam hac de re exponit Robertus Baronius Scotus, dum viveret, in Academia Aberdonensi Professor. Ac ne quid hic supersit obscuritatis & ambiguitatis, distinguit multiplices fiduciae acceptiones, & quatuor hujus vocis significata enumerat. Fiducia, inquit, primo modo accipitur, pro firma persuasione, seu pro firmo & stabili judicio intellectus, quo apud nos statuimus, & propter Dei testimonium in verbo suo credimus, Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, pretioso suo sanguine nos redemisse, & Deum patrem propter ejus meritum, omnia nostra peccata remisisse; eundem etiam, propter illud Christi meritum & sacrificium in cruce oblatum, liberaturum nos ab omnibus hujus vitae miseriis & calamitatibus, & tandem donaturum nos ineffabili illius gloriae aeternitate. Secundo accipitur pro intima acquiescentia in divina benevolentia & gratia, per quam toti ab illa pendemus, non aliunde auxilium salutemve exspectantes. Tertio pro spirituali fortitudine & animositate, qua animi nervos & robur opponimus malis & periculis, sive temporalibus, sive spiritualibus, cum quibus in hac lacrymarum valle conflictamur. Quarto pro pace, tranquillitate, & quasi serenitate conscientiae, seu securitate spirituali, quae quietem a servili timore importat.
pass_a_gloss: But most accurately of all Robert Baron the Scot, while he lived Professor in the Academy of Aberdeen, sets out his mind on this matter. And lest any obscurity and ambiguity remain here, he distinguishes multiple acceptations of trust, and enumerates four significations of this word. Trust, he says, is taken in the first way for a firm persuasion, or for a firm and stable judgment of the intellect, by which we lay down with ourselves, and because of God's testimony in His word believe, that our Lord Jesus Christ by His precious blood has redeemed us, and that God the Father for His merit has remitted all our sins; and that the same, for that merit of Christ and sacrifice offered on the cross, will free us from all the miseries and calamities of this life, and at length will give us the ineffable eternity of His glory. Second it is taken for an inward resting in the divine benevolence and grace, by which we wholly depend on it, expecting help or salvation from nowhere else. Third for spiritual fortitude and courage, by which we oppose the nerves and strength of the mind to evils and dangers, whether temporal or spiritual, with which we conflict in this valley of tears. Fourth for peace, tranquillity, and as it were serenity of conscience, or spiritual security, which brings quiet from servile fear.
pass_b_english: Baron (Aberdeen): four senses of fiducia to clear ambiguity.
1. Firm intellectual persuasion — redeemed by Christ’s blood; sins remitted; future deliverance and glory.
2. Inward rest in God’s goodwill — depend wholly on it.
4. Peace/serenity of conscience — quiet from servile fear.
